requirements.requirement: FixtureSpec validates units, bounds, and coupled feasibility constraints before geometry construction.
requirements.acceptance: Reject negative, nonfinite, out-of-range, and impossible pitch/diameter combinations with a specific explanation.
requirements.rationale: Individually legal dimensions can combine into impossible geometry; reject rather than silently redesign.

requirements.requirement: Every accepted configuration produces exactly two valid, positive-volume single solids.
requirements.acceptance: Inspect each BREP and STEP reimport in a fresh process; reject null, merged, or self-invalid geometry.
requirements.rationale: Pretty meshes are not sufficient evidence of valid editable manufacturing solids.

requirements.requirement: Bore, hole pitches, base thickness, and datums agree with requirements within 0.05 mm.
requirements.acceptance: Independent section/edge/plane queries of reimported STEP measure dimensions.
requirements.rationale: Inspecting exports independently catches generator mistakes and conversion drift.

requirements.requirement: Sensor and connector keepouts remain clear except for explicitly intended contact surfaces.
requirements.acceptance: Boolean intersections and known collision mutations verify the rule and its exclusions.
requirements.rationale: A nominally fitting clamp is unusable if it obstructs the sensor or connector.

requirements.requirement: Fastener and tool-access envelopes remain usable in the prescribed assembly sequence.
requirements.acceptance: Conservative swept tool envelopes identify intentional inaccessible configurations; sampled frames only illustrate the specified straight path and cannot establish clearance.
requirements.rationale: Fasteners need a usable tool path, not just a correctly sized hole.

requirements.requirement: Wall, base, and build-volume requirements are checked on generated geometry.
requirements.acceptance: Deliberately thin or oversized parts fail even if their input metadata claims compliance.
requirements.rationale: Manufacturing rules must be checked against the actual shape rather than trusted input metadata.

requirements.requirement: All six reference designs pass and all eight invalid cases are rejected for their intended cause.
requirements.acceptance: Frozen inventory and explicit case-to-requirement mapping, not just counting nonzero exits.
requirements.rationale: Known invalid designs test whether the geometry inspector catches realistic mistakes.

requirements.requirement: STEP and STL export preserve units and per-part identity; round trips remain within tolerance.
requirements.acceptance: Reimport STEP, compare volume/bounds, and check STL watertightness and triangle orientation.
requirements.rationale: Engineers need interoperable editable geometry and unambiguous units.

requirements.requirement: Offline demonstration shows a rejected candidate and a corrected fixture without a model service.
requirements.acceptance: Run without credentials and network; inspect actual generated CAD and reports.
requirements.rationale: The useful core should work without paid model access.

requirements.requirement: Any generated-code experiment uses bounded isolation and a read-only evaluator.
requirements.acceptance: Timeout, path-escape, and evaluator-write probes fail; JSON-only generation cannot execute code.
requirements.rationale: A generated script must not be able to rewrite the inspector or escape its execution boundary.
requirements.applies_when: Only when executing untrusted generated code; ordinary STEP/JSON inspection must not execute Python from its inputs.

requirements.requirement: Inspection output separates computed geometry from unmeasured physical fit and strength.
requirements.acceptance: Report labels geometric checks, assumptions, and absent physical tests explicitly.
requirements.rationale: Geometric clearance is not evidence of clamping force, print quality, or physical strength.

requirements.requirement: Fresh installation and deterministic inputs reproduce the required artifacts within numerical tolerance.
requirements.acceptance: Record stable versions; compare geometry semantically rather than assuming STEP file bytes are invariant.
requirements.rationale: Kernel versions and numerical tolerance matter more than byte-identical STEP exports.

requirements.requirement: Compare CADCLAW and direct CadQuery/build123d checks on a screw-tool obstruction and connector insertion case before building the checker.
requirements.rationale: The original plan overlaps heavily with an existing open-source project.
requirements.acceptance: Record pinned versions, precise supported checks, actual geometry, and missing behavior in docs/BASELINE.md. If a configuration or small plugin meets the requirements, build that integration rather than a generic CAD validation platform.

requirements.requirement: Check externally authored STEP parts using an explicit AccessSpec JSON without calling the clamp generator.
requirements.rationale: The checker must help engineers with their CAD, not only validate geometry it generated itself.
requirements.acceptance: An independently scripted bracket/connector example imports through the public API and finds one known obstruction. Require mm units, stable part selectors, transforms, tool envelopes, and intended contacts; ambiguous identities or units are an error.

requirements.requirement: For v1, tool and connector paths are fixed-orientation straight translations of supported convex box/cylinder envelopes; test the entire conservative swept envelope.
requirements.rationale: Sampling can miss an obstruction; restricted geometry makes a meaningful full-path check feasible.
requirements.acceptance: Freeze start/end transforms and assembly occupancy per step. A known obstruction between coarse sample positions must be caught. Reject unsupported rotation, curved motion, or failed Boolean geometry as unsupported/inconclusive, never clear. Report nominal clearance and any conservative inflation. Sampled illustrations alone cannot yield a continuous-path pass.

requirements.requirement: Support user-specified tool clearance margins and removal/reassembly sequences with explicit remaining-part occupancy.
requirements.rationale: Different tools and maintenance sequences need different envelopes; avoid claiming universal wrench access.
requirements.acceptance: Changing a margin around a known threshold changes the verdict predictably. Removing a part clears only the documented subsequent steps. Unknown sequence rules are rejected.
requirements.applies_when: If selected after Must requirements pass

requirements.requirement: Compare inspection reports between CAD revisions and locate changed obstruction pairs in a visual view.
requirements.rationale: This makes access constraints useful in everyday design review and CI.
requirements.acceptance: A relocated boss introduces one new tool collision; identify the affected path and parts. A no-change rebuild produces no semantic difference.
requirements.applies_when: If selected after Must requirements pass

requirements.requirement: Add model-proposed FixtureSpec JSON and bounded repair as an optional demonstration after deterministic geometry and access checking work.
requirements.rationale: The portfolio objective is satisfied by a verified agent-built tool, without making model generation a dependency.
requirements.acceptance: Validate model JSON through the same schema and inspector; preserve failed attempts. Freeform code requires separate isolation and is not part of normal import.
requirements.applies_when: If selected after Must requirements pass

requirements.requirement: Publish a versioned input and result schema, stable requirement IDs, public Python API, and a scriptable CLI with clear failure semantics.
requirements.rationale: CI must not confuse an unsupported check or crashed evaluator with a valid result.
requirements.acceptance: For normal check commands: exit 0 only when every applicable required check passes; exit 1 for violations; exit 2 for invalid, incomplete, unsupported, or failed execution. Results preserve individual pass/fail/inconclusive/not_applicable states. The demo command separately verifies its expected negative cases. Unknown schema versions are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Declare resource limits and measure repeatable performance for the supported workload in the pinned environment.
requirements.rationale: A tool that hangs or silently drops large input cannot be trusted in an engineering workflow.
requirements.acceptance: During M0 freeze input-size/case limits and a target runtime with machine details. M4 records actual elapsed time and peak memory; an oversized input or elapsed-time limit produces a bounded error and incomplete result. CAD work runs in a killable worker. Compare against the baseline; do not claim universal performance.

requirements.requirement: Keep offline workflows local by default and document dependency, fixture, manual, and example licensing.
requirements.rationale: Engineers must be able to inspect data handling and legally reuse the code and examples.
requirements.acceptance: No credentials or telemetry are needed; the offline demo completes with egress disabled after installation. Source examples have provenance and redistributable licenses, or use a download recipe and lawful independently authored fixtures. Escape user text in HTML; reject output path traversal and avoid executing input data.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate adoption from a separate clean consumer directory using only the documented public interface.
requirements.rationale: A successful bundled demo alone is not evidence that another engineer can use the tool.
requirements.acceptance: Record a complete cold-start walkthrough: install, configure one non-default input, get an expected failure, correct it, and reproduce success without editing package source. Include actual commands, setup time, code/config size, and limitations versus the baseline. Label agent-executed walkthroughs as such; practitioner validation remains unverified until real feedback exists.

exclusions.requirement: A generic CAD system or replacement for CADCLAW, CadQuery, or build123d
exclusions.rationale: Reuse kernels and inspection capabilities; the differentiator is a bounded access workflow.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: Arbitrary motion planning, articulated wrenches, flexible cable routing, or automatic assembly sequence discovery
exclusions.rationale: A fixed straight path has a tractable geometric contract; general motion planning is a separate project.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: Automatic interpretation of unlabeled STEP intent or arbitrary GD&T drawings
exclusions.rationale: Parts, datums, contact exceptions, units, and access paths must be explicit.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: FEA, machining toolpaths, G-code, or certified DFM analysis
exclusions.rationale: These need process/material models and validation beyond geometric inspection.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: Claims of physical fit, adequate clamping force, strength, or printability without measurements
exclusions.rationale: The 0.05 mm threshold is software inspection tolerance, not manufacturing capability.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

priority_policy.should: Valuable after Must; omission needs an explicit rationale
